correctness.rationale: The quotient shortest-path metric is min(Hamming weight, its complement). The universal zero-sum D_0 identity and N(M^p-1) operator perturbation prove the stated lower bound. The Fourier eigenvalue at a weight-four character is F_d(p)/2 and F_d(0)=-2. The fourth Krawtchouk polynomial and binomial central limit theorem, with explicit uniform integrability on the tails, prove B_d  d^(5/2)/2^d -> sqrt(2/pi). The global Taylor remainder is bounded by (2^d/2)p^2(log M)^2 M^p, vanishing at the proposed critical scale. Thus F_d(p)>0 at all fixed multiples greater than sqrt(2pi) and nesting bounds the negative-type exponent. Finite checks of the character identity and slope were replayed; they are not treated as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The candidate concerns the supremal p-negative-type exponent of the antipodal quotient of the binary Hamming cube, with an exponentially small rate and an explicit fourth-Walsh-mode upper obstruction. Robertson arXiv:2309.16070v1 establishes negative type of unfurled Hamming cubes; Chen--Naserasr--Sarti arXiv:2406.10814v1 identify folded/projective cube graph structures and distances without determining p-negative type. Weston arXiv:0807.2705v1 gives stronger universal lower bounds than the elementary lower estimate here; this lower estimate is not claimed as original. Murugan arXiv:1112.5657v1 and Sanchez arXiv:1108.0451v1 give general finite-metric characterization, but neither states the dimension-uniform 2^(-d+o(d)) rate or the fourth-mode asymptotic constant. Relevant published Rips-complex and Walsh projection records are different invariants. Explicit literature and accessible own-history claim comparisons found no covering statement. Priority remains conditional on as-yet-unindexed equivalents.
residual_risks: Historical priority under a different name for antipodal Hamming metric or generalized roundness may escape indexed queries.
Finite graph spectral tables could imply special small-dimension values, but would not alone imply the asymptotic theorem.
No independent mathematical audit or global novelty certification has been carried out.

value.rationale: This gives a structural and dimension-uniform rate for a canonical graph family: antipodal identification changes maximal negative type from one to exponentially small despite preserving a natural graph quotient metric. A new fourth-Walsh-character obstruction yields an explicit asymptotic coefficient, and a complementary universal perturbation establishes the exact exponential decay rate. It is a motivated, infinite-family metric-embedding result rather than an arbitrary parameter slice or numerical census; it makes no unwarranted claim about the global leading constant.
